items.title: Australia fumes as Israel drops probe into Gaza aid worker killings
items.summary: SYDNEY: Australia's top diplomat said Thursday she was "outraged" by Israel's decision to not pursue a criminal investigation into the killing of Australian aid worker Lalzawmi "Zomi" Frankcom and her colleagues in Gaza. Australia will summon Israel's ambassador Hillel Newman over the move and has asked Canberra's envoy in the country to "convey our views directly" to the government there, Foreign Minister Penny Wong said in a statement "The Australian Government learned of Israel's decision late last night, moments before it was announced, on World Humanitarian Day – which is especially insulting to Zomi's loved ones, humanitarians and all Australians," Wong said. "Zomi represented the best of Australia.

items.title: Immigration lorry tragedy could have been avoided, says road safety activist
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The accident involving an Immigration Department lorry that claimed the lives of a father and his two daughters could and should have been avoided, said a road safety activist. Road Safety Council member Tan Sri Lee Lam Thye said the tragedy raised serious questions over whether there was a need for the Immigration Department vehicle to rush to Chow Kit to pick up detainees following an enforcement operation. "Road safety is everyone's responsibility.

items.title: Los Angeles fire suspect denies charges as prosecution tries again
items.summary: LOS ANGELES: The man accused of starting a fire that grew into one of the deadly blazes that tore through Los Angeles in January 2025 pleaded not guilty Wednesday as authorities made a second attempt to prosecute him. Public prosecutors in America's second biggest city, unhappy about the result, leveled new charges: destruction of property by means of fire and arson affecting property used in interstate commerce. Rinderknecht, who remains in federal custody, denied both charges.

items.title: Police analysing CCTV, dashcam footage
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Police are analysing dashcam and closed-circuit television (CCTV) camera footage in their investigation into an accident involving an Immigration Department lorry that killed a father and his two daughters in Jalan Sultan Ismail early yesterday. A dashcam was installed in the department's lorry. Kuala Lumpur Traffic Investigation and Enforcement Department chief Assistant Commissioner Mohd Zamzuri Mohd Isa said preliminary investigations found that the driver was the only occupant of the lorry during the accident.

items.title: Fatal crash plunges kin into more sorrow [WATCH]
items.summary: KAMPAR: A family still mourning the loss of a loved one just three months ago was plunged into deeper sorrow after a father and his two daughters were killed in the Jalan Sultan Ismail crash early yesterday. Mohd Nadzri Razali, 69, said the latest tragedy had been particularly difficult to bear, coming so soon after the death of his younger sister. I am very sad," he said when met at the family home in Kampar yesterday.

items.title: Beyond the naked eye: What PM2.5, haze’s invisible threat, means for your health
items.summary: PETALING JAYA, Aug 20 — As Malaysians once again experience a resurgence in haze pollution and deteriorating air quality, many have begun taking precautions against its more visible health effects. While coughing, sore throats and irritated eyes may prompt people to take action, some of the more concerning pollutants associated with haze are invisible to the naked eye and may not always factor into how people protect themselves. Known as PM2.5, these microscopic fine particles — particulate matter (PM) measuring 2.5 micrometres or less in diameter — are small enough to penetrate deep into the lungs and potentially trigger adverse health effects beyond the respiratory system.

items.title: Trump to meet North Korea's Kim later this year
items.summary: WASHINGTON: US President Donald Trump said Wednesday that he would meet Kim Jong Un later this year, seeking to revive the bond he claims to have struck with the leader of nuclear-armed North Korea in his first term. Trump told reporters at the White House it was important to "get along" with Kim, adding in an unusually precise assessment that Pyongyang now had 57 "very powerful" nuclear weapons. If I were president, I wouldn't have allowed it," Trump said, referring to Kim.

items.title: Maha back with RM8b trade potential
items.summary: THE Malaysia Agriculture, Horticulture and Agrotourism Exhibition (Maha) 2026 will return from Aug 28 to Sept 6, showcasing technology, innovation and value creation to strengthen the country's food security. Agriculture and Food Security Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Sabu said the theme reflected a broader approach to food security beyond food production. "Food security is not only about food production, but also involves technology, innovation, value creation, entrepreneurship, investment and markets.

items.title: US national debt exceeds US$40 trillion for first time
items.summary: WASHINGTON: The US gross national debt has surged past US$40 trillion for the first time, government data showed Wednesday, outstripping earlier forecasts at a pace fuelled in part by President Donald Trump's invalidated tariffs. Total public debt outstanding stood at US$40.05 trillion at the close of business Tuesday, according to data released Wednesday by the Treasury Department. The increase forces the US government to refinance debt at the highest rates since before the 2008 global financial crisis.

items.title: Ministry builds 2,102 more classrooms for Year One intake
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Education Ministry is implementing 681 projects nationwide to build 2,102 more classrooms to accommodate higher Year One enrolment for the 2027 academic session. According to the ministry, RM668 million has been allocated to build 1,780 classrooms across 524 projects in Peninsular Malaysia and Labuan. In Sarawak, 84 projects costing RM81.5 million are underway to build 210 classrooms, while 73 projects costing RM58 million are being carried out in Sabah for 112 classrooms.

items.title: Trump unveils White House helipad as building frenzy escalates
items.summary: WASHINGTON: US President Donald Trump showed off a giant new helicopter landing pad at the White House on Wednesday, the latest in a series of construction projects, as he seeks to leave his mark on Washington. Trump told reporters. Trump said the granite helipad was necessary because the new versions of the Marine One helicopter coming into service would burn or damage the grass on the iconic lawn at the back of the White House.

items.title: Shiprocket takes off on debut
items.summary: BENGALURU: Temasek-backed Shiprocket jumped as much as 48.6 per cent in its debut trade yesterday, valuing the logistics firm at 100.1 billion rupees as investors bet on its technology-driven model to capitalise on India's fast-growing e-commerce market. India's online retail gross merchandise value is expected to grow at a compound annual rate of 20 per cent to 25 per cent between 2025 and 2030, analysts said. The IPO was subscribed 99.4 times, with retail investors subscribing to 46.4 times their allocation and institutional investors to 122.8 times their allocation.

items.title: Prince Harry and Meghan to move back to UK
items.summary: LONDON: Six years after stepping down as working royals, Prince Harry and his wife Meghan are moving back to the United Kingdom, British press reported late Wednesday. Several UK news outlets including the BBC reported the couple's two children, Prince Archie, 7, and Princess Lilibet, 5, had already been enrolled in a British school for the start of the school year in early September. Harry and Meghan have lived in California since 2020 and the children had not seen their grandfather since 2022.

items.title: Vietnam police break silence on car crash that killed teen
items.summary: HANOI: A former Vietnamese politician unintentionally killed a teenager in a traffic accident in the capital here last year, but was exempted from criminal prosecution, a police officer told state television, shedding light for the first time on a case that has fuelled criticism online for months. Authorities said the accident's exploitation was carried out by "hostile forces". Verified videos shared on social media show people in uniform preventing passers-by from leaving flowers and standing next to a tree, where the accident took place.

items.title: China's robots face a commercial test
items.summary: CHINA'S humanoid robot makers have spent the past two years dazzling investors with machines that can breakdance, throw punches and even set marathon records. The conference coincides with the Shanghai stock market debut of Unitree, one of the world's largest humanoid robot makers by sales volume, after an initial public offering that was more than 8,000 times oversubscribed by retail investors. Unitree founder Wang Xingxing will address the conference's main forum today on the next decade of the humanoid industry.

items.title: Oil market starts pricing in a prolonged Hormuz crisis
items.summary: THE oil market is increasingly behaving as though disruptions to Middle East energy supplies are not a temporary shock but a new reality. US President Donald Trump said on July 7 that the pact was "over". That shift in expectations helps explain why crude oil prices have stabilised around US$90 a barrel.

items.title: NST Leader: GST, SST integration?
items.summary: THE government's willingness to study a combination of the strengths of the Goods and Services Tax (GST) and Sales and Service Tax (SST) is a sensible and pragmatic step — and one that should be welcomed. Instead, the government is looking at how selected GST features could improve the existing SST, with the aim of creating a taxation system that is more progressive and efficient. The question should be simple: What system allows the government to raise sufficient, sustainable revenue while protecting households, particularly lower-income Malaysians?

items.title: Gold mine collapse kills at least 100 people in C.Africa
items.summary: BOUAR, Central African Republic: A landslide at an illegal gold mine has killed at least 100 people in the Central African Republic on the border with Cameroon, the latest of many such accidents in the mineral-rich nation. Search operations are still under way after the accident at the Zamboye mining site, about 50 kilometres (31 miles) from the Central African town of Baboua, on Tuesday afternoon. Several local sources said that around 100 people had died and many others were injured, prompting condemnation from opposition leaders in both countries about artisanal mining conditions.

items.title: Israel army admits firing on car in death of five-year-old Hind Rajab
items.summary: TEL AVIV: The Israeli military on Wednesday admitted its troops fired on a car carrying five-year-old Hind Rajab in Gaza in 2024, saying it had ordered a criminal investigation into the killing which drew international outrage. The Israeli military had previously denied its troops were present in the area near the incident. "Following review of the findings and due to alleged failures in the coordination of the movement of the Palestine Red Crescent ambulance, it has been decided to initiate a criminal investigation of the incident by Military Police Criminal Investigation Division," the military said on Wednesday.

items.title: 11-year-old Thai boy loses more than RM100,000 in Pokémon card scam
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: An 11-year-old boy who claimed to have lost more than one million baht (RM123,000) buying a rare Pokémon card is among at least 25 people from Thailand who alleged they had been duped by a man who promised to source sought-after collectables from abroad. The complainants claimed that the suspect had built a reputation among Thailand's trading card collectors and traders by offering to source rare Pokémon cards and other high-value collectables from abroad. The problems began after customers began placing larger orders, he claimed.

items.title: Factory found flying national, state flags upside down was operating without licence
items.summary: ISKANDAR PUTERI: A factory at Taman Perindustrian SILC here, which had displayed the Jalur Gemilang and Johor flag upside down, was operating without a licence. The Iskandar Puteri City Council (MBIP) said an inspection of the factory today also saw its foreign workers taken to the district police headquarters to verify the status of their work permits. MBIP said the factory was also ordered to cease operations and was closed for failing to comply with MBIP licensing requirements.

items.title: Body found in suitcase may be of foreigner, say Kuala Kangsar police
items.summary: KUALA KANGSAR: Police believe that the unidentified woman, whose body was found stuffed inside a suitcase in Sungai Perak here last Friday, may be a foreigner. District police chief, Assistant Commissioner Heisham Harun, said this was based on the absence of a BCG vaccination scar. Heisham said police have classified the case as murder.

items.title: China commends Anwar's remarks on One-China Principle
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: China has commended Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim for his position on the one-China principle. "Nothing will stop China from being reunified," the China Ministry of Foreign Affairs spokesperson posted on X on Wednesday. "It is one China.

items.title: Today's news in pictures - Wednesday, August 19, 2026
items.summary: MISSED what happened today? Here's a glimpse at what happened throughout the country in photographs. [[nid:1514807]] [[nid:1514806]] [[nid:1514805]] [[nid:1514804]] [[nid:1514803]] [[nid:1514802]] [[nid:1514801]] © New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

items.title: Johor roadside brawl: Singaporean man among two to be charged tomorrow
items.summary: JOHOR BARU: Two men, including a Singaporean, who were involved in a roadside brawl near the Sultan Iskandar Building (BSI) here last week will be charged in court tomorrow. Johor Bahru (South) police chief, Assistant Commissioner Azrul Hisham Mohd Shaffei, said both men would be charged at the Johor Baru Magistrate's Court. Police had previously detained four men, including a Singaporean, aged between 25 and 46, over the incident.

items.title: Indonesian family finds 84-year-old woman alive days after earthquake
items.summary: SIKKA: A paralysed 84-year-old woman has been found alive three days after a strong earthquake flattened her home on an Indonesian island, an official said Wednesday, as the death toll rose to 73. More than 900 people were injured and nearly 60,000 displaced by the 7.7-magnitude quake that struck off Indonesia's Flores island on Saturday, according to the BNPB disaster mitigation agency. Paulina Pobi's house on a small island north of Flores was one of hundreds knocked down by the earthquake, with the 84-year-old buried alive under collapsed bamboo walls.

items.title: Family of 3 killed in Immigration lorry crash laid to rest in Kampar [WATCH]
items.summary: KAMPAR: The remains of a father and his two daughters, who were killed after being struck by an Immigration Department lorry in Kuala Lumpur early today, were laid to rest here tonight. The remains of Shaik Mohd Firdaus Shaikh Yahya, 53, and his daughters, Siti Nor Sazlin, 25, and Siti Darwisyah Auni, 12, arrived at the Kampung Air Hitam Labu Muslim Cemetery at 10.30pm. The talkin and prayers were led by Kampung Air Hitam Labu Mosque imam Yusaini Ariffin.

items.title: ISS hosts first spacewalk by a Frenchwoman
items.summary: WASHINGTON: Sophie Adenot became the first French female astronaut to venture outside the International Space Station (ISS) for a spacewalk on Tuesday, accompanied by American astronaut Anil Menon. Adenot, 44, became the second European woman to conduct a spacewalk after Italian astronaut Samantha Cristoforetti's 2022 mission. "Yeah, what a day," Adenot said after the space walk.

items.title: Woman, 54, killed after being struck by car in Hulu Selangor
items.summary: HULU SELANGOR: A 54-year-old woman was killed after being struck by a car while walking along Jalan Bukit Manchung here this morning. The victim was hit at around 8am by a car driven by a 33-year-old woman who was travelling from Prima Bukit Beruntung towards Kuala Lumpur. Upon reaching Persiaran Bukit Manchung, the car struck the pedestrian, who was walking on the left side of the road.

items.title: Civil Defence Force personnel capture python which swallowed pet cat
items.summary: KLUANG: Civil Defence Force personnel captured a python which had swallowed a pet cat at Kampung Kenangan, Layang-Layang, yesterday. District Civil Defence Force disaster operations unit officer, Mohamad Faizal Othman, said they were alerted to the incident at 5.39pm before deploying an officer and three personnel to the scene. Faizal said the Civil Defence Force had captured 1,230 snakes for the whole of last year.

items.title: 'Ex-minister's aide pressured me for a cut of RM19 million project fee'
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Sessions Court heard from a witness today that he was frequently pressured by Sayed Amir Muzzakkir Al Sayed Mohamad, who was political secretary to a former home minister, to hand over a portion of the RM19 million consultancy fees he received from a police project. The 15th prosecution witness, Al Khairi Group Bhd managing director Datuk Seri Mohd Khairi Mat Jahya, 43, said Sayed Amir Muzzakkir claimed that he had introduced him to the owner of Nexuscorpgroup Sdn Bhd, known as Wan Azhar, and had also arranged a meeting with the then Home Minister, Datuk Seri Hamzah Zainudin. "Sayed also claimed that he had helped Nexuscorpgroup secure the RMPNet project," he said when reading his witness statement during the trial of Sayed Amir Muzzakkir, who faces three corruption charges involving RM350,000.

items.title: MACC urged to clarify status of two-month-old petroleum cargo commingling report
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 19 — Maritime industry observer Datuk Seri Jeyenderan Ramasamy has urged the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) to provide a written update on a report lodged in June concerning the alleged commingling or blending of petroleum cargo. He said the absence of an official response had created a serious operational situation, particularly as decisions involving the handling, movement and management of petroleum cargo could not responsibly be left in indefinite uncertainty. “Decisions affecting the handling, movement and management of petroleum cargo cannot responsibly be left in indefinite uncertainty.

items.title: Shahrir Samad says lawsuit not an act of revenge but to ensure enforcement powers are used properly
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 19 — Former Johor Bahru Member of Parliament Tan Sri Shahrir Abdul Samad told the High Court here today that his lawsuit was not intended as an act of revenge, but to ensure that enforcement powers are exercised appropriately. He said this when testifying in the lawsuit he filed against former Attorney General (AG) Tan Sri Tommy Thomas, former Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) Chief Commissioner Latheefa Koya, the MACC, and the government regarding malicious prosecution. “Those powers must be exercised only after the fundamental aspects have been properly investigated,” said Shahrir, 76, in his witness statement.

items.title: Nga Kor Ming says Malaysia’s ethnic and cultural diversity must be preserved
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 19 — Malaysia’s ethnic and cultural diversity is a national strength that needs to be protected to maintain a harmonious, inclusive and progressive society, Housing and Local Government Minister Nga Kor Ming says. He said the spirit of unity in diversity should remain a driving force for Malaysians, including staff of the Housing and Local Government Ministry (KPKT), to work together in developing the country. Speaking at the launch of Semarak Jiwa Merdeka @ KPKT to mark National Month here today, Nga said the independence Malaysians enjoy today had come at a cost, built on the unity, sacrifices and hard work of the nation’s people.

items.title: Indonesian Navy thwarts bid to smuggle 75.7 tonnes of tin sand worth RM17.27m to Malaysia
items.summary: JAKARTA, Aug 19 — The Indonesian Navy has thwarted a suspected attempt to smuggle about 75.7 tonnes of illegally mined tin sand to Malaysia from the Bangka Belitung Islands off the east coast of Sumatra, with the haul estimated at Rp76.04 billion (RM17.27 million). Indonesian Fleet Command chief Vice Admiral Denih Hendrata said the case came to light after naval personnel intercepted a truck carrying about eight tonnes of tin sand at a jetty in East Belitung on Aug 2, triggering a string of follow-up raids. The raids uncovered about 50 tonnes in Lenggang village on Aug 3, another 10 tonnes packed in 200 sacks the following day and another five tonnes on Aug 8, he said.

items.title: Malaysia’s defence spending driven by emerging threats, not just regional dynamics, says Khaled Nordin
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 19 — The need for higher defence spending was driven not only by regional dynamics but also by emerging threats, said Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin. He said several developments had changed the government’s approach to defence policy and expenditure, including emerging challenges such as cyber and electromagnetic threats, as well as mass misinformation campaigns. This creates a more complex security environment for countries like Malaysia,” he said in a statement today.

items.title: Former 1MDB CEO denies making deal with late lead prosecutor Sri Ram to testify in company’s favour
items.summary: Muhammad Shafee: Did Sri Ram interview you? Shahrol Azral: Yes. Shahrol Azral: Yes, once.

items.title: MOF: Unsubsidised petrol and diesel to rise 10-20 sen per litre from Aug 20-26
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 19 — Retail prices of unsubsidised petroleum products nationwide will increase by between 10 sen and 20 sen per litre for the August 20-26 period, driven by global geopolitical instability affecting crude oil prices and supplies. The price of unsubsidised RON95 will rise by 15 sen to RM3.77 per litre from RM3.62, while unsubsidised diesel will increase by 20 sen to RM4.67 per litre from RM4.47 previously. Prices of subsidised petroleum products remain unchanged, with BUDI Madani RON95 (BUDI95) at RM1.99 per litre and BUDI Madani Diesel (BUDI Diesel) at RM2.10 per litre.

items.title: Home minister orders Immigration to fully cooperate in fatal Maju Junction crash probe
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 19 — Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail has ordered the Malaysian Immigration Department to fully cooperate with authorities in the investigation into the early morning crash involving one of its lorries, which tragically claimed the lives of three family members. Expressing deep sorrow over the tragedy, Saifuddin Nasution also extended his condolences to the family members of the victims. “The entire Ministry of Home Affairs and Malaysian Immigration Department pray that the victims’ family will be given strength and resilience to face this difficult time.

items.title: No Malaysians reported affected by mudslides in northern Chile, says Malaysian rep in Santiago
items.summary: SANTIAGO (Chile), Aug 19 — No registered Malaysians have been reported involved or affected by mudslides following heavy rain in several areas in northern Chile since mid-August, according to the Embassy of Malaysia (Malawakil) in Santiago, Chile today. Malawakil Santiago said as of August 19, a total of 49 Malaysians have registered with the embassy, while it continues to monitor the weather situation in the affected areas. “Heavy rain hit several areas in northern Chile, particularly the Atacama and Antofagasta regions, triggering mudslides,” it said in a report on the extreme weather conditions and flash floods in northern Chile shared with Bernama.

items.title: Kota Bharu hospital says drug‑positive newborn now stable, no longer showing withdrawal symptoms
items.summary: KOTA BHARU, Aug 19 — A baby girl who tested positive for drugs after being born at Raja Perempuan Zainab II Hospital here is now in stable condition and no longer showing withdrawal symptoms. Kelantan Health director Dr Kasuadi Hussin said the baby, who remains under observation at the hospital’s Neonatal Intensive Care Unit (NICU), was showing positive signs of recovery. On August 12, the baby girl tested positive for amphetamine and benzodiazepines after undergoing a urine test at the NICU of the hospital.

items.title: Chairman: MARA reviews MRSM outing guidelines amid probe into disappearance of two Form Four students in Alor Gajah
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 19 — Majlis Amanah Rakyat (MARA) is reviewing the standard operating procedures (SOP) governing outings for students of its Mara Junior Science Colleges (MRSM) following the recent disappearance of two students. Its chairman Datuk Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki said the disappearance of the two Form Four students from MRSM Alor Gajah, Melaka, on August 11 was an isolated case and should not result in rules that could disrupt activities and programmes at MRSMs. The students, both 16, were reported missing on Aug 11 after receiving treatment at a health clinic and were found four days later near Pasar Seni in Kuala Lumpur.

items.title: CM: Penang seeks federal backing for proposed international financial centre in Budget 2027
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Aug 19 — Penang is hoping for its proposed international financial centre (PIFC) to be approved under Budget 2027. Chief minister Chow Kon Yeow said the state hopes to pitch the proposed PIFC to the Finance Ministry with the white paper prepared by an appointed consultant. He said the PIFC could eventually be known as the Penang Technology Financial Centre, to better reflect its intended purpose of financing technology development in the state.

items.title: Securities Commission: Putrajaya to determine whether RCI’s oversight recommendations for Tabung Haji will be adopted
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Aug 19 — The federal government will decide whether the Securities Commission Malaysia (SC) should regulate Lembaga Tabung Haji’s (TH) fund management and investments, SC chairman Datuk Mohammad Faiz Azmi said today. He said the proposal was among recommendations made by the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) and is being examined by a task force involving Bank Negara Malaysia (BNM) and TH. Mohammad Faiz said such oversight was appropriate given the scale of TH’s investments.

items.title: Over 127,000 scam‑related posts removed, mostly from Facebook and TikTok, says Fahmi
items.summary: Government spokesman Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said the issue included fake content such as information on the Sumbangan Asas Rahmah (SARA) programme that was not announced by the Finance Ministry. He said the fake content amounted to 27 per cent of the total content that was requested to be taken down. The communications minister said most such accounts use platforms such as Facebook and TikTok for scam activities.

items.title: Police advise Malaysian motorcyclists and drivers entering Thailand to comply with local laws
items.summary: KOTA BHARU, Aug 19 — Malaysian motorcyclists and motorists entering Thailand are advised to comply with local laws there to avoid enforcement action. Kelantan police chief Datuk Mohd Yusoff Mamat said road users should first familiarise themselves with the regulations in Thailand, as there are differences in laws between the two countries. They must obey our laws,” he told a press conference at the Kelantan Contingent Police Headquarters today.

items.title: HR Ministry to review TalentCorp processing times for Malaysian doctors seeking to return home
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 19 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has ordered the Human Resources Ministry to review and report back to the Cabinet on the status of current applications from Malaysian doctors who want to return to work in the country. Government spokesman Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said the ministry was directed to examine several aspects related to applications that are under Talent Corporation Malaysia Berhad (TalentCorp). “This also covers applications from doctors who want to return to Malaysia to serve”.

items.title: Serian tops Sarawak’s unhealthy API readings as seven areas exceed 100 at 4pm
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 19 — Seven areas in Sarawak recorded unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings as of 4pm today due to transboundary haze. Meanwhile, 55 areas in the state recorded moderate API readings of between 51 and 100, while six others recorded good air quality levels (below 50). API data is released hourly based on readings from 68 air quality monitoring stations nationwide.

items.title: Anwar orders full study of hybrid SST-GST system, report to go to Cabinet
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 19 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has directed the Finance Ministry to conduct a full study on the proposal to introduce a hybrid taxation system that combines the current Sales and Services Tax (SST) with the Goods and Services Tax (GST). Government spokesman Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said Finance Minister II Datuk Seri Amir Hamzah Azizan has been tasked with overseeing the study of the hybrid taxation system’s suitability. He said the government also has yet to make a decision on the proposed hybrid taxation system.

items.title: Family of victims wants full probe, justice after father and two daughters killed in Maju Junction crash in KL
items.summary: KAMPAR, Aug 19 — A family member of the victims involved in the early morning crash involving a Malaysian Immigration Department lorry on Jalan Sultan Ismail is calling for a full and transparent investigation to ensure justice is served for his loved ones. Mohd Nadzri Razali, 69, brother-in-law of the late Shaik Mohd Firdaus Shaikh Yahya, 53, said he heard that the lorry allegedly ran a red light at the accident site. He said his younger sister Norhayati Razali, 55, is still being treated in the Intensive Care Unit of Kuala Lumpur Hospital.

items.title: Fahmi: New legislation to replace UUCA will exclude provisions affecting student freedom
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 19 — The new legislation that will replace the Universities and University Colleges Act (UUCA) 1971 will not restrict the freedom of students or undergraduates. Government spokesman Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil assured that the new legislative Bill will instead focus on the administration and management aspects of universities as well as university colleges. He said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim had told the Cabinet that matters involving students and undergraduates will be excluded following the government’s intention to abolish UUCA 1971 as announced last weekend.

items.title: Finance Ministry witness says PMO involved in Jana Wibawa procurement process, but no order to select KCJ Engineering
items.summary: Today, Zamzuri referred to Muhyiddin’s November 13, 2020 letter to the finance minister, which contained a list of 54 proposed companies for 54 proposed Jana Wibawa projects, including KCJ Engineering Sdn Bhd. At that time, Zamzuri was secretary of the Finance Ministry’s government procurement division. Based on this list, Zamzuri agreed that the PMO was involved before the process to evaluate contractors for three of the Jana Wibawa projects, which were eventually awarded to KCJ Engineering Sdn Bhd, Nepturis Sdn Bhd and Sutracom Sdn Bhd.

items.title: Police probe whether stress played role in Hulu Selangor teacher’s death
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Aug 19 — Police are continuing investigations into the death of a female teacher who was found unconscious at a school in Hulu Selangor late last month. Selangor Police chief Datuk Shazeli Kahar said investigators were examining various factors, including whether stress played a role, in the case which has so far been classified as a sudden death report (SDR). Separately, Shazeli said police were investigating allegations that a workshop in Kampung Bukit Kapar, Klang, which had been linked to foreign nationals suspected of dismantling and selling vehicle parts, was set on fire to destroy evidence.

items.title: Sandakan declares fire disaster after 28 homes destroyed on Pulau Nunuyan Laut
items.summary: SANDAKAN, Aug 19 — The Sandakan District Disaster Management Committee (JPBD) today declared a fire disaster in the district following a blaze that destroyed 28 houses at Pulau Nunuyan Laut early this morning. Sandakan JPBD chairman Datuk Walter Kenson said the declaration was made at 9am based on reports and information received from agencies on the ground. In a statement here today, he said a temporary relief centre (PPS) was opened at Masjid Al Fattah, Kampung Nunuyan Laut, at 10am following the declaration.

items.title: Haze eases for now, but could return within days, says MetMalaysia
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 19 — Humid weather over the past few days has helped ease haze in the Klang Valley and Sarawak, but conditions could deteriorate again in the near future. Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) director-general Mohd Hisham Mohd Anip said hot and dry conditions were expected to return within days, with the country still in the Southwest Monsoon season until the end of September. During the Southwest Monsoon, lower humidity contributes to reduced rainfall and more days without rain, Mohd Hisham said.

items.title: ‘No need to escalate’: Selangor police urge public against gathering at court over Rocky case
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Aug 19 — Selangor police chief Datuk Shazeli Kahar today reportedly urged the public not to hold a gathering when a man linked to the death of a dog named Rocky appears in court tomorrow, saying the legal process is already under way. According to The Star , Shazeli said police had completed their investigation, identified those responsible and received instructions for charges to be brought. He reportedly said members of the public who wished to witness the proceedings could attend as the court’s public gallery would be open.

items.title: KL police identify father and two daughters killed in Maju Junction crash; nephew says family was visiting relatives
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 19 — Police have identified the three family members killed in the early morning crash involving a Malaysian Immigration Department lorry on Jalan Sultan Ismail. Kuala Lumpur Traffic Investigation and Enforcement Department chief ACP Mohd Zamzuri Mohd Isa said they were Shaik Mohd Firdaus Shaikh Yahya, 53, and his two daughters, Siti Nor Sazlin, 25, and Siti Darwisyah Auni, 12. Also present was Kuala Lumpur Immigration director Hamsha Injau.

items.title: Ahead of Budget 2027, higher education students call for expanded assistance to manage rising living expenses
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 19 — Ahead of the tabling of Budget 2027, higher education students are hoping the government will expand financial assistance to help them cope with rising costs of living. Besides increases to existing aid such as Sumbangan Tunai Rahmah (STR) and Sumbangan Asas Rahmah (SARA), students are calling for new measures to ease their daily expenses. Increasing National Higher Education Fund Corporation (PTPTN) loans was not a complete solution, he said, calling on the government to provide targeted assistance or subsidies to help cover education and living costs without adding to students’ financial burden after graduation.

items.title: Shah Alam police receive report on Form Three student at risk of hearing loss after alleged bullying
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Aug 19 — Police have confirmed receiving a report regarding an incident involving a Form Three student who claimed to have been bullied to the extent of being at risk of hearing loss at a secondary school here last week. Selangor police chief Datuk Shazeli Kahar said the 17-year-old suspect had been detained and released on police bail pending completion of investigations. Yesterday, the media reported that a Form Three male student had suffered injuries to his neck and nape and was at risk of hearing loss after allegedly being bullied and assaulted at a secondary school here last week.

items.title: Quizzed on China-Taiwan relations, Anwar says he would use force if needed to prevent Malaysia from breaking up (VIDEO)
items.summary: KUCHING, Aug 19 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim believes he would use force to prevent any province from breaking away from the Federation of Malaysia. Sreenivasan: So, you would use force? Anwar: Yes.
